champion: Giant Cell Tumor of the Tendon Sheath
ordered_diagnoses: Giant Cell Tumor of the Tendon Sheath

s1.syndrome_frame: A slowly enlarging, painful mass on the wrist
salient_findings: A firm, tender mass on the dorsal aspect of the right wrist
The mass moves with extension of the right index finger
Ultrasound shows a well-defined, multilobulated, mildly echogenic swelling
key_facts: The patient is a 4-year-old girl
The mass is located on the dorsal aspect of the right wrist
The mass was first noted 2 months earlier
The mass causes pain and discomfort
There is no history of trauma
The mass is firm and tender
The overlying skin is intact
Wrist range of motion is normal
Sensation is intact
Pulses are palpable
The mass is located medial to Lister’s tubercle
Ultrasound shows a well-defined, multilobulated, mildly echogenic swelling
The swelling is mildly echogenic and has some vascularity
